extra.solution: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

In some cases, this may even result in a user gaining complete control of the session of another user, depending on the configuration of the caching components in use in their environment. This is primarily an issue where caching servers such as "proxy" caches are configured on the local network. This configuration is typically found in corporate or educational environments, for instance.

extra.solution:
Validate that the response does not contain sensitive, personal or user-specific information. If it does, consider the use of the following HTTP response headers, to limit, or prevent the content being stored and retrieved from the cache by another user:
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, private
Pragma: no-cache
Expires: 0
This configuration directs both HTTP 1.0 and HTTP 1.1 compliant caching servers to not store the response, and to not retrieve the response (without validation) from the cache, in response to a similar request.

correlate.executive_summary: The assessment identified several security weaknesses on juiceshop.cortexlab.org.in. Most notably, an exposed /ftp path hosts multiple discoverable files (including what appears to be an incident-support.kdbx) that may contain sensitive data. Multiple missing/insufficient security headers (Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, HSTS) and a suspected CORS misconfiguration increase risk of client-side attacks and information leakage. Nmap detected indicators of HTTP-level DoS issues (byterange overlap / Slowloris) and a phpMyAdmin LFI check, but these are not confirmed against a clearly matching product/version (the site is fronted by a Cloudflare proxy).

findings.title: Exposed /ftp directory with discoverable files (possible sensitive data)
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 200 on /ftp (body hash differs from baseline) ; va (zap): numerous files enumerated under /ftp and /ftp/quarantine (e.g. incident-support.kdbx, juicy_malware_*.url, package.json.bak) ; nmap (http-robots.txt): robots.txt lists /ftp as Disallow.

findings.title: Missing / inconsistent security response headers (CSP, Referrer-Policy, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
findings.evidence: va (zap): 'Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set' (confirmed) and 'Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set' (confirmed) reported across many endpoints; recon: response lacked content-security-policy and referrer-policy and flagged missing strict-transport-security; nikto: reported X-Frame-Options header not present for one endpoint while nmap http-security-headers output included X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN (conflicting observations).

findings.title: Cross-origin / CORS misconfiguration (cross-domain resource risks)
findings.evidence: va (zap): 'Cross-Domain Misconfiguration' flagged across many endpoints (suspected) ; nmap (http-cors) listed allowed methods (HEAD GET POST PUT DELETE PATCH) — indicates CORS/allowed methods information present but no complete verification of unsafe Access-Control-Allow-Origin values was captured.

findings.title: Potential HTTP DoS indicators: Apache byterange (CVE-2011-3192) and Slowloris behaviour (CVE-2007-6750) reported by nmap
findings.evidence: nmap: http-vuln-cve2011-3192 reported 'State: VULNERABLE' for Apache byterange overlapping ranges (cites CVE-2011-3192) ; nmap: http-slowloris-check reported 'State: LIKELY VULNERABLE' and references CVE-2007-6750. Note: nmap/recon also detected a Cloudflare HTTP proxy in front of the host; live CVE lookups for the detected Cloudflare proxy failed and the scans did not produce a confirmed matching product/version for an Apache origin, so these remain unconfirmed indicators.

findings.title: phpMyAdmin grab_globals local file inclusion check (CVE-2005-3299) - unable to verify
findings.evidence: nmap: http-phpmyadmin-dir-traversal script output references 'PHP file inclusion vulnerability in grab_globals.lib.php' and cites CVE-2005-3299 but notes 'State: UNKNOWN (unable to test)'. No explicit phpMyAdmin product/version fingerprint captured by scanners.

findings.title: Cache-control directives and shared cache retrieval observed
findings.evidence: va (zap): 'Re-examine Cache-control Directives' reported missing/incorrect cache-control on many resources (suspected); va (zap): 'Retrieved from Cache' observed for robots.txt indicating response was served from a shared cache — may risk leaking sensitive responses if caching is misconfigured.

findings.title: Site fronted by Cloudflare proxy (technology fingerprint)
findings.evidence: nmap service/version detection: 'http (Cloudflare http proxy)' on ports 80/443/8080/8443 ; recon: 'Detected: cloudflare.'

correlate.deduplication_notes: Merged multiple agent reports about the same underlying issues: (1) recon's discovered /ftp and robots.txt entries were combined with va's enumerated /ftp file listings and nmap's robots.txt output into a single exposed /ftp finding; (2) multiple missing-security-header observations from recon, va (zap) and nikto/nmap were consolidated into one security-headers finding, with a note about conflicting X-Frame-Options evidence; (3) nmap's DoS-related NSE outputs (http-slowloris-check and http-vuln-cve2011-3192) were combined into a single DoS indicators finding and annotated to reflect that CVE applicability is unconfirmed because the service was detected as Cloudflare proxy and live CVE lookups did not produce confirmed matches; (4) cache-control and 'retrieved from cache' zap findings were combined. Items that were purely informational or duplicate NSE script checks (various http-* NSE info results) were not elevated to separate findings.
